PullRequest.Title: sessions: add cloud automations to the composer dialog

## Summary

Wave 4 of the cloud automations stack, targeting `bevillal/cloud-automations-routing` (#339419), not `main`. Adds the cloud create/edit dialog experience and workspace pickers on top of the wave 3 routing. Everything stays behind `chat.automations.cloud.enabled` (default off) and the parent Automations / AI-disabled gates.

**Choosing a cloud target**
- The workspace picker offers **Work in GitHub**. It reuses the New Chat repository search, shows only private repositories, and accepts a pasted repository URL. Picking a repository selects Cloud and keeps a matching local checkout as the displayed workspace.
- Local folders backed by an eligible private GitHub repository can choose Cloud directly from the session type picker. Other supported agents remain selectable; the execution provider is independent of the displayed workspace.
- Repository eligibility is checked per selected folder, at most 5 checks at a time, and cached until refresh or account change. Known public repositories hide Cloud for new automations, and a draft on Cloud falls back to Copilot when it switches to a public repository. Network failures never silently switch providers, and writes still revalidate on the server.
- When editing an existing cloud automation, the workspace picker is disabled because the repository and provider can't change; duplicating is the path to a new target.

**Form**
- Order is Target, Prompt (with the cloud model picker), Tools, then Schedule. There's no Enabled checkbox; editing preserves enabled state, and cards remain the place to enable or disable.
- **Tools** section: "Select which tools the agent can use. Built-in tools are always available." plus a **Configure allowed tools** button. It opens the shared quick tree picker, populated from the Mission Control tool catalog (`GET /agents/automations/tools`) with the server's groups, names, and descriptions. The catalog is loaded on demand, cached per account session, and shows loading, error, and Retry states without blocking the dialog.
  - New automations start with every catalog tool selected, and saving waits for the catalog if needed.
  - Saved tool IDs outside the catalog are shown under **Other Saved Tools** and preserved.
  - If GitHub didn't report saved tools on edit, they're left untouched.
- Schedules are shown and edited in local time and saved as GitHub's fixed UTC schedule; minutes off GitHub's quarter-hour grid are blocked with an inline message.
- With Cloud selected, a note beside Create reads "Runs even when your computer is off, triggered on a schedule."
- Escape inside the dialog now closes quick inputs (including the repository search) instead of being swallowed.

**Shared changes (minimal)**
- `IAutomationProviderConfiguration` and `IAutomationWorkspaceTarget` describe provider-owned dialog configuration and checked targets.
- `RepositoryPicker` takes an optional placeholder.
- `getGitHubRepositoryId` moved to `githubUrls.ts` so both pickers share it.
- `_findRelatedLocalWorkspace` is protected so the automation picker can reuse matching.
- New pure `automationScheduleToLocal`/`ToUTC` helpers.

## Scope and deferred work

Cards, run history/navigation, and native-session adoption are left for later waves. Repository discovery is limited to the user's known/recent private repositories; no account-wide scan. No changes to the API client contracts introduced in wave 1–3.

Open questions for the tool catalog: whether it includes the legacy IDs (`read`, `edit`, `bash`, `github/*`) is unverified, and new automations rely on built-in tools being always available server-side.

## How to test

1. Enable `chat.automations.cloud.enabled`, sign in to GitHub.com, open the Agents window and go to Automations.
2. **New Automation**: pick **Work in GitHub** → search for a private repo; Cloud is selected. Switch the folder to a public repo: Cloud disappears from the session type picker and the draft falls back to Copilot.
3. With Cloud selected, open **Configure allowed tools**, check the groups from the server, toggle a few, press Enter; Escape cancels without closing the dialog.
4. Pick a local time, create, and confirm the definition on GitHub has the matching UTC trigger. Reopen it: local time shows, the workspace picker is disabled, and enabled state is unchanged after saving.
5. With the feature off, or with a local agent selected, the dialog is unchanged.

## Validation

At head `65ad8fc1d28` (single commit on wave 3 at `fbb266ac94c`):

- `npx tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck`: passed.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --runGlob '**/{automationDialog,automationsView,cloudAutomationStore,githubCloudAutomationStore,copilotChatSessionsProvider,sessionTypePicker,sessionWorkspacePicker,repositoryPicker,schedule,automations.contribution}.test.js'`: **651 passed**.
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob` (same glob, Electron): **648 passed, 4 pending**.
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files, Stylelint on `automationDialog.css`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and commit hygiene hooks: passed.

Earlier in the branch, live validation in Code OSS against GitHub created two temporary disabled automations in a private repo to verify local-to-UTC conversion (09:45 PDT → 16:45 UTC; Sunday 23:45 PDT → Monday 06:45 UTC), then deleted them. That was before the move to the Mission Control base. **The Mission Control tool catalog and the rebased dialog have not yet been validated end to end against the live service.**

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path, one-request-per-cache-miss implementation, five-request limiter, and mobile `Promise.all` wait are directly traced in repository code. Exact network duration varies, but the fan-out and critical-path reachability are deterministic for cold cached GitHub recents.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One `client.query.getRepository` request is queued for every distinct GitHub remote workspace returned by `_buildItems`; the current picker commonly exposes up to 10 recents, and the limiter runs five at a time, so a cold mobile open requires multiple network waves.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excess network traffic on every cold dialog lifetime and delayed mobile workspace-picker opening.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, constructing or opening the automation workspace picker did not preflight repository visibility; the existing cloud-store refresh already checked known repositories separately.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: `setCloudConfiguration` now installs an autorun during dialog construction that walks every picker item and calls `getWorkspaceTarget`, whose cache miss immediately queues a remote visibility read. The mobile path additionally waits for all of those targets before rendering the sheet.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call `value?.getWorkspaceTarget(item.item.folderUri).read(reader)` at line 2183 is inside a loop over all picker rows and is installed eagerly by the newly added `setCloudConfiguration` call during form rendering.
Findings.Title: Defer repository eligibility checks until a repository is selected
Findings.Impact: With several remembered GitHub workspaces, merely opening the automation dialog launches a burst of visibility requests even if the user never opens the workspace picker. If a mobile user opens it before those requests finish, the sheet remains busy until all requests complete; 10 recents execute in two batches because concurrency is capped at five.
Findings.Evidence: `renderForm` immediately calls `workspacePicker.setCloudConfiguration(...)`; this added autorun loops over `super._buildItems()` and invokes `getWorkspaceTarget` for every GitHub row. `GitHubCloudAutomationStore.getWorkspaceTarget` creates a cache entry and queues `client.query.getRepository(...).private` on a `Limiter(5)` for each miss. `waitForWorkspaceTargets` then uses `Promise.all` over the same collection before mobile rendering. The recent picker is capped at 10 in the current layout, while the cloud store's existing refresh already performs visibility reads for known repositories, so these are additional per-dialog-lifetime requests rather than reuse of refresh results.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not call `getWorkspaceTarget` for every recent row during dialog construction or wait for the full collection before showing mobile UI. Validate only the selected row through the existing `_dispatchPickerItem` path, or defer/background row checks after the picker is visible and reuse eligibility established by the store refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the create/edit automation dialog and open its workspace picker with cloud automations enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Desktop dialog rendering and picker display do not await eligibility, but the new autorun starts eligibility work during form construction. On mobile, `showReadyMobilePicker` awaits every GitHub workspace target before showing the sheet, so all cold visibility checks are on the picker-open critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each workspace to a repository and call `client.query.getRepository(...).private`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct cold GitHub workspace row, commonly up to 10, grouped five concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the automation dialog/picker did not perform per-row eligibility reads. The pre-existing store refresh separately checked known repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background traffic for desktop dialog opening; the full set blocks mobile workspace-sheet display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct GitHub remote rows returned by the workspace picker. The current layout commonly caps displayed recents at 10; legacy composition can include additional fallback workspaces. Effective remote cardinality is deduplicated by the target cache key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `GitHubCloudAutomationStore.targetEligibilityLimiter` permits five visibility operations at once. Ten cold rows therefore require two request waves; repeated reads for the same URI coalesce through the map.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold dialog lifetime fans out across remembered GitHub rows; warm rows reuse map entries. Refresh/account invalidation makes the next observation cold again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the eager loop, cache-miss request, five-wide limiter, and mobile `Promise.all` wait are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual latency depends on the number of GitHub rows and network RTT, but multiple remembered repositories and two limiter waves are realistic. This uncertainty supports medium rather than high severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the diff adds avoidable per-row network fan-out and places completion of the whole batch on mobile picker-open latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Work in GitHub and search for a private repository
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository authentication completes before the quick picker opens. The initial repository search and each settled query must complete before selectable results are shown. After selection, the chosen repository's eligibility check must complete before applying the workspace.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticate for repository access and call `gitHubService.getRepositories` for the current query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial call plus one call for each query that remains unchanged for 300 ms; superseded requests are cancelled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The automation dialog had no Work in GitHub repository-search path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication blocks opening; each latest query blocks result availability.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Verify the selected repository is private.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call for a cold selected repository; zero on a warm cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cloud repository target selection existed in this dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selection waits for verification before the target is applied.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User query changes and one selected repository. A 300 ms scheduler coalesces typing; changing the query cancels the prior request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one active repository-search request per picker because `requests.clear()` cancels the previous token. The selected repository then uses the shared five-wide eligibility limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Search responses are not retained by this change; in-flight searches are cancelled/coalesced by the shared picker. Eligibility of the selected URI is cached per store, including success and terminal error/public states until refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: debounce, cancellation, selection wait, and eligibility cache are directly implemented.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication and GitHub search duration vary, but cardinality is bounded and query cancellation is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the search is user-requested, debounced, cancellation-aware, and selection performs one necessary cached validation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select Cloud, configure tools, and save a new or existing cloud automation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selecting Cloud starts tool-catalog loading without blocking the dialog. Opening the tools tree requires the ready catalog. Saving a new cloud automation with default-all tools waits for the catalog; edits with unreported tools preserve them without waiting. Commit then reaches the provider mutation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful request per account/store lifetime; a failed request can be retried explicitly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dialog had no provider tool-catalog request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the dialog-open path; on the save critical path only for a new cloud automation saved before its default tool set is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate repository visibility and create, or revalidate plus fetch/update, the automation definition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One visibility check plus one create request; updates perform one visibility check, one authoritative get, and at most one update, serialized per store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud mutations and server-side repository revalidation already existed; the diff only supplies dialog metadata/tool choices to them.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tool groups/tools returned once for the account session, then one selected automation mutation. Tool-tree construction is linear in catalog tools and deduplicates IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `loadTools` coalesces while loading and does nothing once ready. Store mutations are serialized through a sequencer. No per-tool network calls are made.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tool success is cached until account/client/store reset; loading is coalesced; errors are retryable rather than permanently negative-cached. Selected tool IDs are held only for the dialog lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: load guards, account reset, save wait, and serialized mutation path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size is service-controlled, but there is one response transformation/tree allocation rather than per-tool I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: expensive work is on demand, coalesced per account, and bounded to one catalog request plus the existing mutation sequence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render automation cards/accessibility text and edit schedules
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Schedule conversion and formatting run synchronously while cards/accessibility content or the dialog are rendered, but perform only fixed arithmetic and date-offset lookup per schedule.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered automation cards; constant work per schedule.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local computation; no queue or parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed; conversion is constant-time and allocates one small schedule object only for UTC daily/weekly schedules.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: helper implementation is pure arithmetic with no transitive I/O.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the work is constant and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added local-time projection does not create a meaningful CPU, allocation, rendering, or boundary regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 25 changed files and traced dialog construction, workspace selection, repository search, tool-catalog loading, cloud save, refresh invalidation, and schedule rendering. Submitted one medium-confidence boundary-fanout finding: dialog construction eagerly starts per-recent repository visibility checks, and mobile picker opening waits for the entire batch.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
